card.intuition: An agent mode is a preset bundling a permission mode with behavioral instructions injected into the system prompt - plan mode blocks edits and steers the agent toward research, bypass permissions (YOLO) auto-approves everything. The gate decides what runs; the instructions decide what the agent wants to run.
card.analogy: A kitchen with roles: the rule that salads plate before desserts stops the line from skipping ahead, and the station note telling the garde manger to prep first steers the work - together they shape the whole shift.
card.time_complexity: Every tool call costs an extra model provider request, because the tool result must go back to the model before it can decide what to do next - modes change how calls get gated, not the round-trip structure.
card.space_complexity: Injected behavioral instructions live in the system prompt, and modes can flip mid-session, so the instructions and accumulated tool results all share the finite token budget.
when_to_use: When you want a plan, not edits - switch to plan mode so it reads, asks, and proposes instead of straining against a gate
When trust grows over a task - escalate from plan to default to accept-edits to bypass as the agent proves it understands the change
When running AFK - use bypass mode, but only inside a sandbox
gotchas: A gate alone produces an agent that wants to edit but can't; the injected instructions are what remove the want
If you approve every prompt without reading it, the mode is set tighter than your actual trust
Changing mode mid-session is free - the conversation continues exactly where it was

steps.label: Preset
steps.annotation: An agent mode bundles a permission mode with behavioral instructions injected into the system prompt.

steps.label: Gate
steps.annotation: The permission part decides which tool calls are blocked, asked about, or run freely.

steps.label: Steer
steps.annotation: The injected instructions remove the want - plan mode never reaches for the write tool.

steps.label: Flip
steps.annotation: You change mode as trust changes; the conversation continues exactly where it was.

steps.label: Match
steps.annotation: If you accept every prompt without reading, the mode is tighter than your actual trust.

exercise.prompt: Build an agent mode preset that bundles a permission gate with behavioral instructions for the system prompt.
hints: The instructions in the system prompt steer behavior so the agent doesn't strain against the gate
accept-edits mode auto-approves edits, so the instruction should allow editing
exercise.test_code:
assert build_mode('plan')['gate'] == 'read_only'
assert 'planning' in build_mode('plan')['instructions']
assert build_mode('accept-edits')['instructions'] == 'You may edit files freely.'
assert build_mode('bypass')['gate'] == 'bypass'
print('PASS')
